results.reason: Item 1 says §9.4(c) disapplies the cap and basket for all §9.2(a) claims, leaving every rep breach uncapped beyond the $1.84M escrow. It recommends limiting the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and preserving fraud.

Item 4 flags the TSA's Delaware law and forum, the split-forum risk, and recommends conforming to New York. However, it never explains that APA §10.12 lets the TSA control its own subject matter, so the conflict is not cured. The §10.12 analysis appears only in the Bill of Sale discussion.

Item 2 shows the BoS definition has no Excluded Asset carve-out and conveys cash, Albany and HOLLIS. It notes the BoS may control under §10.12 and recommends adopting the APA definition with express exclusions.
States the 10% cap ($1,840,000) and links it to the escrow.
Names cash, the Albany manufacturing facility and the HOLLIS trademark.
It is a memo, and each item gives the Where/section, the issue and its significance to the seller, and a Fix.
Issues are ordered 'Most Significant First' with severity labels, and Section 4 is a separate list of business decisions.
The memo argues §10.12 may let the BoS definition win and proposes narrowing §10.12. It never says §10.12 cures either conflict.
The memo concludes rep breaches are uncapped, not limited to the cap or escrow.
